name: Big Sugar Creek
difficultyRating: Class I–II (floatmissouri.com, for the Elk/Big Sugar system: "mostly II, seldom over")
description: A small, very clear Ozark creek in McDonald County that flows west down Sugar Creek Valley through Powell and Cyclone and joins Little Sugar Creek at Pineville to form the Elk River. About 24 guide miles are floatable, from the Hwy 90/KK bridge in high water down to the confluence, but the only agency-verified public access on the creek is MDC's Deep Ford Access, about 4 miles above Pineville. Rain-driven and flashy: it runs a few cubic feet per second in early autumn and has crested above 30,000 cfs.
managingAuthority: No agency manages the creek corridor. MDC owns and manages Deep Ford Access; the City of Pineville maintains the Elk River access below the confluence under an MDC cooperative agreement; private outfitters and campgrounds control their own landings. Big Sugar Creek State Park (Missouri State Parks) borders the valley but publishes no creek access.

regulations.text: Deep Ford Access: camping is prohibited. Area open daily 4:00 AM–10:00 PM; boat launching (and hunting, fishing, trapping where permitted) allowed 24 hours a day.
City of Pineville Elk River Access (Elk River, below the confluence): city-maintained under an MDC cooperative agreement; follow posted MDC/city area rules.
regulations.authority: City of Pineville / Missouri Department of Conservation

regulations.text: Big Elk Floats & Camping (private, Pineville): private boats on Big Sugar are offered a boat shuttle only ($40 per boat); the operator states it cannot vehicle-shuttle for Big Sugar. Children under 3 are not allowed to float with the operator.

accessLaw.value: Missouri follows the "navigable in fact" doctrine: the public may float and wade streams navigable in fact, but streambeds and banks are frequently privately owned, so portaging or camping on private gravel bars and banks can be trespass. Navigability is decided stream by stream; there is no statewide list. On Big Sugar Creek, use MDC Deep Ford Access, the City of Pineville Elk River Access, or an operator landing under its published terms. This dossier does not infer launch, parking or camping permission from a road crossing, low-water bridge, gravel bar, or the historical floatmissouri.com/Hawksley guide (which calls Cyclone "good access"; a 2018 reader comment on the same page reports private property and restricted parking there).

gauges.name: Big Sugar Creek near Powell, MO
gauges.knownBias: At Powell (floatmissouri guide mile ~5.5), roughly 9 guide miles above Cyclone and ~15 guide miles above Deep Ford; Mikes Creek, Kings Valley, Little Cedar Hollow and other small tributaries enter between the gauge and the recommended corridor. moherp logged a 'Good' Deep Ford→Elk trip at only 48 cfs here (2014-11-10), so the lower reach may float at lower Powell readings than the upper reach. Do not transfer Powell numbers to the Elk or Little Sugar.

sections.name: Lower Big Sugar Creek: Deep Ford Access to Pineville (Elk River)
sections.description: Recommended initial corridor: MDC Deep Ford Access (guide mile 20.4) down Big Sugar to the Little Sugar confluence (guide mile 24.3), then ~0.26 mi on the Elk to the City of Pineville Elk River Access. moherp logs this as a 4.1-mile trip. It is the only pair with agency-verified public access at both ends, and it crosses rivers: the take-out sits on Eddy's Elk river record (Elk mile 0.26), so planner routing across the confluence must be built and validated before the pair is offered. Upstream reaches (Powell and Cyclone to Deep Ford) are documented in the access list but held until legal launch evidence exists.

characteristics.lowWaterMeaning: Gravel riffles drag. moherp OBSERVED: 'Low' (significant dragging, possible portages) begins at 50 cfs and 'Good' at 80 cfs at Powell; a 39 cfs trip was rated Low. USGS daily medians at Powell fall to roughly 24 cfs on Aug 1, 15 on Sep 1 and 11 on Oct 1 (descriptive only; percentiles are not thresholds). No signed-off cutoff.
characteristics.risingWaterHazards: Rain-driven and flashy. NWS (BSGM7) action stage 8 ft (~2,190 cfs), minor flood 10 ft (~3,500 cfs); record crest 24.69 ft / 30,900 cfs on 2013-08-08. Several low-water bridges, including Crag O' Lea about half a mile below Deep Ford, become pinning hazards as water rises. No floater do-not-float number is published.
characteristics.rainLagNote: No published rain-to-rise lag for this creek; not researched beyond the NWS crest history.
characteristics.dropRateNote: Unknown; moherp trip notes contrast a fast 341 cfs float with a 'much slower' 182 cfs float one week later (2020).

Flash flooding: NWS flood categories at Big Sugar Creek near Powell (BSGM7): action 8 ft (2,190 cfs), minor 10 ft (3,500 cfs), moderate 15 ft (9,400 cfs), major 20 ft (19,850 cfs). Historic crests include 24.69 ft / 30,900 cfs (2013-08-08) and 22.78 ft / 21,200 cfs (2015-12-27). Cross-check only; these are not floater limits.

localKnowledge: Pineville is the base. Big Elk Floats & Camping sits on the Elk just below the confluence and runs a $40-per-boat shuttle for private Big Sugar boats. Sugar Island Camp & Canoe (1354 Big Sugar Creek Rd) is a long-running creek outfitter whose own website could not be reached.
Deep Ford Access prohibits camping. Overnight stays need a private campground; gravel bars and banks are commonly private.

Water is exceptionally clear. A 2018 Memorial Day account reported paddlers had the creek to themselves while Elk River lots were packed (https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2018/jul/03/stream-s-beauty-dazzles-paddlers-on-big/).

Seasonality (inference from USGS daily medians at Powell against the moherp observed floor): median flow is about 92–146 cfs from March through May, falls below 50 cfs by July and to about 11 cfs in early October. Expect spring and early summer floats; late summer and early autumn are often too low at Powell.
Big Sugar Creek State Park borders the valley but is a trail park; it publishes no creek launch.

legalAccess.notes: Verified public: Deep Ford Access (MDC page: gravel canoe/kayak launch, parking, camping prohibited, 4 AM–10 PM, launching 24 h) and City of Pineville Elk River Access (MDC cooperative page; already approved on the Elk). Held: Cyclone, Powell, Hwy E, Crag O' Lea and Roller bridges — road crossings with no permission source; a 2018 comment reports private property and restricted parking at Cyclone. Operators: Big Elk publishes a $40/boat Big Sugar shuttle but names no put-in; Sugar Island's site was unreachable. Big Sugar Creek State Park publishes no creek access.

conditions.notes: Recommendation: UNRATED (readings-only). moherp OBSERVED at Powell gives only floors (Low ≥50, Good ≥80 cfs) from 7 trips; no High, Flood or do-not-float level exists from moherp, outfitters or American Whitewater. A floor-only ladder would grade every reading from 80 cfs to the 10 ft flood-stage override (~3,500 cfs) 'Good' on a creek that has crested at 30,900 cfs. Candidate floors are kept in research notes for a future rated release. moherp ESTIMATED values (930/410/171/70/19) and USGS percentiles are rejected. Requires owner sign-off of the unrated mode.

hazards.notes: Known on the recommended trip: Crag O' Lea low-water bridge ~0.5 mi below Deep Ford; channel split at guide mile 23.9; wing dikes near Pineville (2015 article); flash floods (NWS action 8 ft, minor 10 ft; record 24.69 ft / 30,900 cfs). Upstream: low-water bridges at Cyclone (14.6) and near Mikes Creek (6.8). No dam found in consulted sources, which is not the same as confirming none exists. Strainer reports are unverified (forum unreachable). Remaining: position each structure, confirm passage/portage facts, and record an evidenced hazard table. Never claim hazard-free.
